title: Affine deformation chart after removing the strict transform
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Using affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], set $X=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and $J=(I,t)$. In the blow-up [def-nagata-global-blowup] of $X$ along the closed subscheme $V(J)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform] of the closed subscheme $V(t)$ is empty on the $t$-chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$. On the $f_i$-chart, writing $C=R[I/f_i]$ and $v=t/f_i$, the strict transform is the closed subscheme $V(v)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C[v]$, and its complement is the overlap with the $t$-chart. Consequently the complement of the strict transform in the blow-up is covered by, and over $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ is identified with, the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$, where $R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$ is the subalgebra generated by $R[t]$ and the elements $f/t$ for $f\in I$.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), 080D (definition-strict-transform); affine specialization to the centre (I,t), with schematic closure calculated by the kernel on each chart

proof.text: Put $A=R[t]$ and write $P=\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. On the singleton affine cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the global blow-up is the affine local model by the definitions of the global blow-up, its gluing datum and its local model. The affine chart isomorphism and chart cover give opens $U_t=\operatorname{Spec}A[J/t]$ and $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A[J/f_i]$ covering $P$. In the homogeneous Rees presentation, with auxiliary degree-one symbol $z$, their images are $D_+(tz)$ and $D_+(f_i z)$. The chart map sends $xz/(az)$ to $x/a$. By the definition of the chart algebra as a subalgebra of $A_a$, $A[J/t]=R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; explicit affine calculation

proof.text: Fix $f=f_i$ and set $C=R[I/f]\subseteq R_f$. By the chart-ring definition, $A[J/f]$ is the subalgebra of $R_f[t]$ generated by $R$, $t$, all $f_j/f$, and $t/f$. Substitution $v\mapsto t/f$ identifies it with $C[v]$: its image contains these generators because $t=fv$, and conversely they all lie in the image. It is injective because a relation $\sum c_n(t/f)^n=0$ in $R_f[t]$ gives $c_n/f^n=0$ coefficientwise, hence $c_n=0$ in $R_f$ and in its subring $C$. This also applies when $R_f=0$, when both rings are zero.

source.place: Tag 052Q, definition-blow-up; explicit substitution in the chart subalgebra

proof.text: Let $H=V(t)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its strict transform $T$ is the schematic closure of $H$ pulled back away from $V(J)$. This closure may be computed on each of the displayed opens: apply restriction of scheme-theoretic image to the immersion of the open part into $H\times_X P$. This immersion is quasi-compact, since locally its source is the finite union of the principal opens defined by $t,f_1,\ldots,f_m$, and is quasi-separated since it is an open immersion. The image definition identifies the closure ideal on an affine chart with the kernel of restriction to that open part. Regard its closed immersion into $H\times_XP$ also as a closed subscheme of $P$, using $H\times_XP=V(t)$ chartwise.

In $U_t$, every $f_j=t(f_j/t)$, so the extended centre ideal is $(t)$. Thus the part away from the centre is $D(t)$. Its intersection with $V(t)$ is the empty scheme; its schematic closure in $V(t)$ is empty since the kernel of the map to the zero ring is the whole ring. Therefore $T\cap U_t=\varnothing$ scheme-theoretically.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; explicit affine calculation

proof.text: In $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C[v]$, the extended centre ideal is $(f)$, because $t=fv$ and $f_j=f(f_j/f)$. Hence the open part of $H\times_XU_i$ used for the closure is $V(fv)\cap D(f)$. Since $C_f=R_f$ (both inclusions follow from $R\subseteq C\subseteq R_f$ and adjoining $1/f$), its coordinate ring is $R_f[v]/(v)=R_f$. Its map from $C[v]$ sends $v$ to $0$ and is the inclusion $C\hookrightarrow R_f$ on constants. Consequently its kernel is exactly $(v)$: the constant coefficient of a kernel element vanishes in $R_f$, hence in $C$, and every polynomial with zero constant coefficient is a multiple of $v$. The closure ideal computed in Step 3 is therefore $(v)$, and $T\cap U_i=V(v)$ as a closed subscheme of $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; explicit affine calculation

proof.text: Inside $U_i=D_+(fz)$, the open $U_i\cap U_t$ is $D(v)$. Indeed under its standard-open identification, the degree-zero fraction $(tz)/(fz)$ is $t/f=v$. A homogeneous prime not containing $fz$ contains $tz$ if and only if its corresponding localized prime contains this fraction. Thus restriction to $D_+(tz)$ is precisely restriction to $D(v)$, with its open-subscheme structure. Here the chart map's fraction formula fixes the actual coordinate and not just an abstract isomorphism. By Step 5 the complement of $T$ in $U_i$ is consequently this overlap.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; explicit affine calculation

proof.text: The opens of Step 1 cover $P$. Step 4 puts all of $U_t$ in $P\setminus T$, while Steps 5-6 put $(P\setminus T)\cap U_i$ inside $U_t$ for every $i$. Therefore $P\setminus T=U_t$ as open subschemes. The identification in Step 1 is over $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and gives the asserted affine scheme and all the claimed chart complements.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NJ-b56b3d875 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all seven steps in full, every cited node's statement, the parent def-pur-dnc-section-family, and Stacks Tag 0804 (divisors.tex l.8322), Tag 080D (l.8781) and Tag 01R8 (morphisms.tex l.849). The delivery adds no new nodes. Step 1: the singleton-cover blow-up is the local model, the chart cover by t,f_i is correct, and A[J/t]=R[t,I/t] holds because (f+tg)/t=f/t+g. Step 2: A[J/f]≅C[v] is injective since 1/f^n is a unit in R_f and C⊆R_f. Step 3: the closure is computed chartwise by restrict-open (01R8(3)); the map is quasi-compact because D(J) is a finite union of basic opens. Step 4: the extended centre on U_t is (t), so T∩U_t is empty. Step 5: (C[v]/(fv))_f=R_f, so the kernel is (v). This agrees with the 080D torsion form, since f^N c_0=0 in C forces c_0=0. Step 6: the overlap is D(tz/fz)=D(v) via θ. Step 7: the cover gives P\T=U_t over Spec R[t]. Edge cases checked: m=0, f_i nilpotent, I=R, zero-divisor generators, R=0. No duplicate: the generic Nagata strict-transform-chart nodes could have been cited but are not needed. The item does not restate the parent. No SGA is cited.
